item.title: Guwahati Hosts Launch of Debut Historical Fiction Anthology "Colour My Grave Purple"
item.description: Guwahati witnessed the launch of debut author Shehnab Sahin’s first book, Colour My Grave Purple, published by Niyogi Books under its English fiction imprint, Olive Turtle. The book, an anthology of 10 historical fiction stories, traces Assam’s socio-cultural and political journey across more than a century, spanning from 1858 to 2019. item.title: Myanmar Goes to Polls on December 28, Five Years After Coup-Critics Doubt Democracy’s Return
item.description: GUWAHATI: Myanmar goes to the polls on Sunday, December 28, marking the first phase of a general election after a five-year gap—an exercise that critics argue will do little to revive the country’s shattered democracy or halt the brutal civil war unleashed by military rule. item.title: Deepti Sharma Becomes Third-Highest Wicket-Taker in Women’s International Cricket; First Indian to Reach 150-Mark in T20
item.description: GUWAHATI: India all-rounder Deepti Sharma has registered multiple milestones during the third T20 International against Sri Lanka, moving to third place on the list of highest wicket-takers in women’s international cricket. The spell also saw Deepti become the first Indian cricketer, across both men’s and women’s formats, to reach 150 wickets in T20 Internationals. item.title: PAN–Aadhaar Linking Deadline Set for December 31; Inoperative Status Looms for Non-Compliant Holders
item.description: GUWAHATI: The Income Tax Department has issued a renewed reminder to all Permanent Account Number holders to link their PAN with Aadhaar before the stipulated deadline of December 31. Failure to complete the linking process within the prescribed timeline will result in the PAN becoming inoperative, impacting multiple tax-related services. item.title: KV Maligaon Alumni Meet Draws Participation from India and Abroad
item.description: Former students of Kendriya Vidyalaya Maligaon came together on Saturday, December 27 for the Pan KV Maligaon Alumni Meet, drawing participation from alumni based across India and abroad. The event served as a reunion for past batches and an opportunity to reconnect with teachers and the school community. item.title: Kaziranga Sees Rise in Foreign Tourists with Over 6.6 K Footfall Till December 27
item.description: GUWAHATI: Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve has recorded a strong surge in tourist arrivals in the 2025–26 season, with a notable rise in foreign visitors. As per official data up to December 27, the park welcomed 1,46,157 tourists, including 6,699 foreign nationals.
